chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Hamid said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the door through which one exits to al-Safa, for our companions differed regarding it among themselves; some of them said it is the door that faces al-Siqayah, and some of them said it is the door that faces the Black Stone. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the door that faces the Black Stone, and the one that faces al-Siqayah was made by Dawud and opened by Dawud.'

key_terms.السِّقَايَةَ: Al-Siqayah (a place or structure in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: Which door leads to al-Safa according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith resolves a practical juristic dispute among early companions regarding the specific entrance to al-Safa, with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirming the door facing the Black Stone as the normative path. By attributing the construction and opening of the alternative door to Prophet Dawud (AS), the narration links current ritual practice to prophetic precedent, reinforcing the continuity of sacred geography in Shia fiqh. This clarification underscores the importance of adhering to the Imam's guidance in resolving minor variations in ritual execution.
